overall_summary: Analysis of the recent 7-day performance data reveals that space exploration, extreme astronomical 'What If' scenarios, and planetary curiosities (such as liquid diamond, burning ice, and extreme exoplanets) are driving the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and comment engagement for FACTVERSE. Conversely, older psychological and straightforward brain-fact shorts are underperforming with negligible engagement. The audience clearly favors high-concept speculative astrophysics with strong visual hook structures.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 970 to 1,024 views with high like counts (up to 38 likes) within days of publishing.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, hypothetical survival scenarios in extreme cosmic environments, focusing on vivid, sensory-rich physical consequences.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) outperformed other recent uploads with over 700 to 1,000 views and strong like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing lesser-known exoplanets with extreme, counter-intuitive meteorological or optical phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s) stalled below 20-50 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Pause standard self-help or generic psychological fact videos unless framed as a high-concept, uncanny scientific mystery.
